newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Air Moldova starts twice-weekly service ex-Schiphol.
newsitem.headline: Air Moldova starts twice-weekly service ex-Schiphol.

text.p: Air Moldova starts twice-weekly flights from Amsterdam Schiphol to Moldova on April 14.

Rolf Florentinus, cargo manager of Aviation World MAK, Air Moldova's Benelux general sales agent, said the service will be operated with a Yakolev 42D aircraft which has a capacity of 3,500 kilograms.
Flights will depart from Schiphol on Mondays and Fridays. Air Moldova hopes to add a third weekly flight in the summer, he told Reuters.
The service will fly to the Moldovian Republic's capital, Kishinev with onward connections to the Ukranian city of Dnepropetrovsk.
Although the Yakolev's are Chapter 3 aircraft, Air Moldova is consdiering replacing the aircraft with B737-300 aircraft and currently negotiations are taking place with Boeing, said Florentinus.
Aviation World MAK has represented Air Moldova in the Benelux since last October. The handler at Schiphol will be Ogden Aviation.
Air Moldova also flies from Frankfurt airport five times a week.
Cargoes include flowers, agricultural machinery, computers and medicines from the Netherlands and agricultural products, wine and trucks are imported from the Moldova Repulic into western Europe.

The Dutch GSA also represents Air Europe which operates services to the Caribbean, Tanzania, Kenya and the Maldives for its freight activities. Vietnam Airlines is also a client of the GSA but this is on the passenger side only. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
